in_hebrew.name: חסד
in_hebrew.meaning: חסד הוא שם שפירושו חסד, טוב, וחמלה בעברית
in_hebrew.long_meaning: חסד הוא שם שמקורו בתנ"ך העברי, ופירושו חסד, טוב, וחמלה. הוא נגזר מהמילה 'חסד' שפירושה חסד אלוהי, טוב, ורחמים. השם חסד מופיע מספר פעמים בתנ"ך, ומשמעותו היא התגלות של חסד אלוהי וטובו כלפי בני האדם. השם חסד הוא שם נפוץ בקרב יהודים ונוצרים כאחד, ומשמעותו הרוחנית היא התגלות של חסד אלוהי וטובו.

in_greek.name: Χεσέδ
in_greek.meaning: Χεσέδ σημαίνει καλοσύνη, έλεος και συμπόνια στα Ελληνικά
in_greek.long_meaning: Χεσέδ είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από την Εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει καλοσύνη, έλεος και συμπόνια. Στο Χριστιανισμό, το όνομα Χεσέδ συνδέεται με την έννοια της θείας καλοσύνης και του ελέους. Το όνομα Χεσέδ δεν εμφανίζεται άμεσα στη Νέα Διαθήκη, αλλά η έννοια της καλοσύνης και του ελέους είναι κεντρική στο μήνυμα του Ευαγγελίου.

in_latin.name: Chesed
in_latin.meaning: Chesed significat misericordia, bonitas, et clementia in Latino
in_latin.long_meaning: Chesed est nomen Hebraeum quod significat misericordia, bonitas, et clementia. In traditione Christiana, nomen Chesed coniungitur cum conceptu misericordiae et bonitatis divinae. Quamvis nomen Chesed non appareat directe in Scripturis Latinis, notio misericordiae et bonitatis est centralis in doctrina Christiana.

in_english.name: Chesed
in_english.meaning: Chesed means kindness, mercy, and goodness in English
in_english.long_meaning: Chesed is a Hebrew name that means kindness, mercy, and goodness. It originates from the Hebrew word 'chesed,' which signifies God's loving-kindness, mercy, and goodness towards humanity. In Christian tradition, Chesed is associated with the concept of divine mercy and goodness. Although it does not appear directly in the Bible, the concept of chesed is central to the biblical message of God's love and redemption. The name Chesed conveys spiritual meaning, personality traits of compassion, and kindness, and is used across Christian cultures.

biblical_reference.note: The concept of chesed appears throughout the Hebrew Bible, emphasizing God's covenantal love and mercy.

data.cultural_impact: The concept of Chesed has had a profound impact on Jewish culture, influencing the way Jews relate to one another and to the world around them. It is reflected in the many Jewish practices and customs that promote acts of kindness and charity, such as tzedakah (charitable giving), Gemilut Hasidim (acts of loving-kindness), and the concept of Tikkun Olam (repairing the world).
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of Chesed lies in the understanding that God's love and mercy extend to every aspect of creation, and that we are called to emulate that love in our own lives. By practicing Chesed, we are not only fulfilling God's commandments and demonstrating our faith, but we are also deepening our connection to the divine and to one another. The Talmud teaches that "as the body is nourished by food, so is the soul nourished by acts of loving-kindness." By performing acts of Chesed, we not only help to repair the world, but we also nourish our own souls and draw closer to God.
